body:
# the contributor audit of section-tail consequences and scalar rigidity

The arithmetic equality classification passes independent inspection.
For d>1 strict convexity of the positive-part L_d increment is applicable
at every argument used in both the initial step and the barrier recurrence.
For d=1 the exact square-root quadratic gives precisely rho=1/2 as the
arithmetic equality shift. Equality for a general tail additionally forces
every term of its arithmetic upper envelope to be present, hence the full
odd-multiple suffix. The exact rationalized deficit formula and the
noninteger mean of a full odd profile are correct. Its verifier passes.

The stationary-section theorem passes with the correction identified by
the independent measure audit: every section-moment integral, not only
the scalar masses s_z, must be restricted to original positive d-volume
fibers. The revised note makes that restriction explicit. For n=1 the
omitted fibers can only truncate the ends of the positive section support,
so the remaining consecutive masses still have concave (d-1)th roots.
Applying the scalar theorem yields the exact gamma_d section-side bound.
The parameterization has isometric restrictions to integer fibers and the
derivative coarea factor is 1/|u|, with no integer-normal factor.

The moving-tilt identities have the correct signs. The right-side
derivative is -S_+ + a'T, while the left-side derivative is -S_- - a'T.
The revised cap-integral formula gives the required chain rule and
absolute continuity with the stated regularity. Integration controls
the side masses only after retaining the displayed torque corrections.

The concentric-disk example realizes the optimized profile as
A_2(t)+2A_1(t) for t>0 and compares all continuous normal directions,
all integer tilts, and closed vertical competitors. Thus the selected
caps really are global normal minima at their stated points. The
second derivative tending to positive infinity near t=1 disproves
every positive-power concavity of this optimized profile.

The square-product example also has a complete global cap lower
certificate: its contained centrally symmetric slab has twice the
claimed cap mass. The oblique cap with parameters b=1/2,a=-9/20 has
right-integer-side fraction 11/30, below gamma_2. The smooth tilted
family has derivatives -6,4,-12 for the total, right and left parts.
Its exact verifier passes. Neither a single stationary section nor
the optimized normal by itself removes the integration correction.

These statements still do not bound an initial cap by the requisite
fraction of the entire mixed measure. No OC proof is inferred.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
